title: py_ntcpx v1.1.1 — a reproducible NTCP modelling and machine learning pipeline for radiotherapy dose–volume data

creators.name: Mondal, K.
creators.affiliation: North Bengal Medical College, Darjeeling, India

description:
py_ntcpx is a reproducible, end-to-end pipeline for normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) modelling from radiotherapy dose–volume histograms. It takes cumulative DVH exports and a clinical covariate table and produces per-patient NTCP predictions, calibrated performance metrics, publication-ready figures and tables, and model explanations, under a single deterministic run. The reference application is Grade ≥2 xerostomia following parotid irradiation in head and neck cancer, but the pipeline is organ- and endpoint-agnostic.

Four-tier evaluation framework

Every cohort is evaluated across four escalating levels of model complexity, so that modern methods are always reported against a classical baseline on identical data:

  • Tier 1 — Legacy-A: QUANTEC Lyman–Kutcher–Burman and relative-seriality models at fixed published parameters.
  • Tier 2 — Legacy-B: LKB and relative-seriality models refitted to the cohort by maximum likelihood.
  • Tier 3 — Modern classical: multivariable logistic NTCP combining dosimetric and clinical predictors.
  • Tier 4 — Machine learning: artificial neural network, XGBoost and random forest, with SHAP attribution, uncertainty NTCP and the Cohort Consistency Score.

Modelling

  • Classical radiobiology: LKB probit and log-logistic, relative-seriality Poisson, and generalised equivalent uniform dose (gEUD), at QUANTEC parameters or refitted locally.
  • Uncertainty quantification: probabilistic gEUD and Monte Carlo NTCP propagate parameter uncertainty to per-patient credible intervals.
  • Full DVH metric extraction (V5–V70, D0.01–D98, mean, max and minimum dose, effective volume).

Evaluation and reporting

  • Calibration: Brier score, expected and maximum calibration error, reported alongside discrimination.
  • Honest validation: leave-one-out and k-fold cross-validation with all preprocessing fitted inside each fold; every model is refit on the full cohort before apparent performance is reported.
  • Overfitting diagnostics: a single documented four-level scheme (NONE / MODERATE / HIGH / CRITICAL) grades the gap between apparent and cross-validated performance for every model.
  • Explainability: SHAP attribution with bootstrap stability analysis, and LIME explanations for individual patients.
  • Cohort Consistency Score: a Mahalanobis-based measure of how representative each patient is of the cohort, published with ccs_specification.json recording the metrics used, the covariance treatment and the provenance of its threshold.
  • QA reporting: automated consistency and integrity checks across every pipeline stage.

Pipeline

Twelve stages run under a single entry point, with a contract validator asserting the expected schema between stages: DVH preprocessing, clinical reconciliation, DVH plotting and summary, biological DVH generation, NTCP analysis with machine learning, QUANTEC stratification, tiered analysis, QA reporting, clinical factor analysis, publication diagrams, SHAP analysis and publication tables.

Reproducibility

Every stochastic component — the Monte Carlo samplers, SHAP bootstrap resampling and LIME — is explicitly seeded, so repeated runs on the same input are bit-identical. requirements.txt pins the complete environment to the exact versions used to produce the published results, and the pipeline completes all twelve stages under it.

Data availability

The accompanying data archive is keyed on anonymised identifiers PT001–PT054. No patient name, hospital identifier or exporting user appears anywhere in it, and the identifier mapping is deliberately not distributed.
